Welcome to the Adventure 
 
Congratulations! You’ve just picked up a book that’s going to 
change the way you think about business and teach you real 
world strategies to help you be successful.  
But don’t worry, it’s not one of those boring textbooks filled with 
corporate jargon and soul-sucking spreadsheets.  
We’ve all read enough of those, and after a while, it’s just not fun 
any more, and one thing that I have discovered through my life is 
that business doesn’t have to be boring!  
No, my friend, this is an adventure.  
And not just any adventure, your adventure. 
This is a gamebook, a thrilling, dice-rolling, decision-making, 
strategy-driven journey where you’ll go from an eager 
entrepreneur with a dream to a business powerhouse with a 
thriving empire.  
Along the way, you’ll make choices, take risks, roll dice to 
determine outcomes, and, if you play your cards right, walk away 
with a newfound understanding of what it actually takes to build a 
successful business. 
Whether you’ve always wanted to start a business but never 
knew where to begin, or you’re already on the path but feel like 
you’re one marketing mistake away from living in your mom’s 
basement, this book is for you.

pages.rawText:
You’ll not only learn business essentials, you’ll experience them, 
make mistakes, adapt, and (hopefully) come out victorious. 
How This Works 
Think of this book as part strategy game, part business 
simulator, and part “oh wow, I actually learned something” 
experience.  
Every time you turn the page, you’ll be making real business 
decisions, facing challenges, and rolling dice to see whether your 
choices lead to triumph or disaster. 
At the start, you’ll create your character, an up-and-coming 
entrepreneur with different strengths, weaknesses, and starting 
resources.  
Then, as you progress through the game, you’ll: 
●​ Pick a mentor to help guide you through each phase of 
your journey. 
●​ Make critical business decisions that will impact your 
success. 
●​ Roll dice to determine the success or failure of key 
actions. 
●​ Face random events (because life loves throwing 
surprises at entrepreneurs). 
●​ And choose different paths based on your playstyle, 
whether you’re a sales-driven closer, a marketing genius, 
or a networking master. 
Each time you play, your experience will be different depending 
on the choices you make, the mentors you select, and how lucky 
(or unlucky) you get with the dice. Some runs will end in riches 
and glory.

Others… well, let’s just say there’s always a chance you’ll go 
bankrupt and have to start over.  
But hey, failure is just a stepping stone to success, right? 
And failing in this book as part of a game comes with a lot less 
risk before you experiment in the real world!  
What You’ll Need to Play 
Before we dive in, let’s go over the essentials you’ll need to get 
the most out of this experience: 
●​  A Character Sheet – You can use the one provided at 
the back of this book, make your own on paper, or 
download one from our website. This is where you’ll track 
your stats, resources, and progress. 
●​ Dice (or a Dice App) – You’ll be rolling two six-sided 
dice (That’s 2d6 in nerd speak) throughout the game. 
Don’t have physical dice? No worries, there are plenty of 
free dice-rolling apps online. 
●​ A Pencil  – You’ll need to update your character sheet as 
you progress.  
●​ A Sense of Humor – Because, let’s be honest, business 
is unpredictable. Sometimes, you launch a marketing 
campaign, and it takes off like a rocket. Other times… You 
accidentally set your ad budget to $10,000 a day and 
watch your savings evaporate before lunch. Laugh, learn, 
and keep playing!

Who This Book Is For 
●​ Aspiring Entrepreneurs – If you’ve ever thought, I want 
to start a business, but I have no clue what I’m doing, 
you’re in the right place. 
●​ New Business Owners – Already started but feeling like 
you’re winging it? This book will help you think more 
strategically and make better decisions. 
●​ Marketing Enthusiasts – If you love learning about 
branding, ads, and sales but want an interactive way to 
test your knowledge, this book will keep you hooked. 
●​ People Who Just Love Games – If RPGs, strategy 
games, or choose-your-own-adventure books are your 
thing, you’ll love this mix of storytelling, 
decision-making, and dice-driven gameplay. 
How to Win (Or Lose) the Game 
There’s no one way to “win” in business, and the same goes for 
this game. Your goal is to grow your business, survive 
setbacks, and ultimately reach your first $10k success. 
However, you’ll face unexpected challenges that could make or 
break you.  
Bad investments, marketing flops, competitors stealing your 
ideas, sound familiar?  
Luckily, you’ll also have mentors, resources, and game 
mechanics that can turn things around… IF you play smart.

pages.rawText:
Your Journey Begins 
You stare at the blinking cursor on your laptop screen, hands 
hovering over the keyboard. This is it, the moment where you 
take the leap from dreaming about being your own boss to 
actually making it happen. No more excuses. No more “I’ll start 
tomorrow.” Today is the day you begin building your empire. 
But let’s be honest: You have no idea what you’re doing. 
You’ve read the success stories, seen the flashy Instagram posts 
of entrepreneurs sipping lattes in Bali, and binged enough 
motivational videos to fill a TED Talk marathon. But deep down, 
you’re still wondering, how do people actually make money 
online? 
The good news? That’s exactly what you’re about to figure 
out. 
The bad news? It won’t be easy. 
Starting a business is like stepping onto a roller coaster that you 
built yourself while blindfolded. There will be highs, there will be 
lows, and at times, you’ll feel like the whole thing is about to come 
crashing down. But that’s what makes it exciting, right? 
You imagine the possibilities, working from anywhere, making 
money doing something you love, proving all the doubters wrong.  
9

pages.rawText:
But then reality hits: How do you even start? 
Do you register an LLC? Build a website? Buy a course from a 
guy who promises you’ll be making six figures in a month if you 
just ‘DM 100 people a day’?  
You grab your notebook and scribble down some ideas.  
Maybe you’ll sell a product, offer a service, start a YouTube 
channel, or create an app. The options are endless, but one thing 
is clear, you have to pick a path and take action. 
As you take a deep breath, the excitement starts to outweigh the 
fear.  
You’re not just playing a game, you’re learning real business 
skills that could change your life.  
And the best part?  
You’re in control of your own story! 
Your adventure begins now and it's time to take the first step… 
 
Who You Are (Character Creation) 
 
Before you can conquer the business world, you need to define 
who you are as an entrepreneur.  
This is where character creation comes in, your strengths, 
weaknesses, and starting resources will shape your journey.

pages.rawText:
Are you a marketing genius who can sell anything but struggles 
with organization?  
Or a networking pro who thrives on connections but has zero tech 
skills?  
The choices you make here will influence your gameplay. 
Step 1: Rolling Your Stats 
Your character is defined by five key stats that shape your 
business journey. Roll 1d6 (one six-sided dice) for each stat and 
record the results on your character sheet: 
●​ Creativity (CR)  – How innovative you are at generating 
new marketing ideas and strategies. 
●​ Tactics (TA)  – Your ability to close deals, negotiate, and 
execute under pressure. 
●​ Resilience (RE)  – How well you handle setbacks, 
criticism, and failure. 
●​ Networking (NE)  – Your skill in forming connections, 
attracting influencers, and building partnerships. 
●​ Tech Savviness (TS)  – Your ability to master online 
tools, funnels, and paid ads. 
If your rolls leave you with a particularly weak stat, don’t worry, 
every entrepreneur has strengths and weaknesses!  
Your mentor choices and business strategies will help you 
navigate these challenges. 
Step 2: Choosing a Bonus Perk 
After rolling stats, you can choose one Bonus Perk to give 
yourself an advantage in a specific area:

Step 3: Choosing Your Mentors 
Throughout your journey, you won’t be going it alone. Before 
each stage in your business, you’ll have the chance to choose a 
mentor, a seasoned entrepreneur who can provide guidance, 
strategies, and unique bonuses to help you succeed. 
Each mentor brings special skills, advantages, and knowledge 
that cater to different playstyles.  
Some might focus on sales, others on branding, and some on 
automation or paid ads.  
The right choice depends on your business strategy and 
playstyle. 
The Mentor Pages section at the back of the book contains their 
full backgrounds, skills, and abilities! 
Turn to the mentor section to choose your mentor for act 1! 
With your stats, perk, and mentor decided, you’re now ready to 
start your business adventure!

pages.rawText:
Act 1: The Struggling Startup 
 
1. The Call to Adventure 
The fluorescent lights of your office flicker above you, a constant 
reminder that you’re still here, trapped in the same lifeless 
cubicle, scrolling through social media while your boss thinks 
you're working on a quarterly report. Another entrepreneur just 
posted about making six figures in their sleep. Someone else 
launched a simple product that went viral overnight. And here you 
are, sipping cold coffee and wondering if there’s more to life than 
emails marked "urgent" that somehow never seem that urgent. 
Then, it hits you. You could do this too. You’ve got ideas. 
Maybe even a great one. What’s stopping you from launching 
your own business and taking control of your future? You sit up 
straighter, adrenaline buzzing through your veins. It’s time to 
make a move. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Quit your job immediately and go all in! → Go to 2 
●​ Side hustle while keeping your job. → Go to 3 
●​ Buy a “Get Rich Quick” course from a guru. → Go to 4

pages.rawText:
2. The Leap of Faith 
You close your eyes, take a deep breath, and before you can talk 
yourself out of it, you do it. You draft the resignation email, hit 
send, and lean back in your chair. A wave of adrenaline rushes 
through you. No more bosses. No more meetings. No more 
wasted time. 
By the time you walk out of the office for the last time, reality 
starts creeping in. No more steady paycheck, either. You have 
savings, but it won’t last forever. Now, the clock is ticking. 
Back home, you sit in front of your laptop, staring at a blank 
screen. What’s your next move? 
●​ Start building a website and brand identity right away. 
→ Go to 5 
●​ Figure out who your audience is and what they 
actually need. → Go to 6 
●​ Go straight into selling something, figure out the 
details later. → Go to 7 
 
3. The Cautious Climb 
You decide to play it safe. You’re not ready to give up the comfort 
of a steady paycheck just yet. Instead, you commit to working on 
your business during evenings and weekends. It’s going to be 
exhausting, but at least you won’t be homeless if things don’t 
work out.

pages.rawText:
Each night after work, you pour over YouTube tutorials, marketing 
blogs, and startup success stories. You start making slow 
progress, sketching out your ideas and mapping out a plan. But 
balancing work and a side hustle isn’t easy. Your boss is starting 
to notice your decreased enthusiasm at work, and your social 
life? Well, let’s just say your favorite streaming service has 
started asking if you’re still alive. 
What’s your next step? 
●​ Focus on learning and planning before taking any big 
risks. → Go to 8 
●​ Test the waters by offering a service or selling a small 
product. → Go to 9 
●​ Take out a small loan to speed up the process. → Go 
to 10 
4. The Shortcut Gamble 
Scrolling through social media, you stumble across an ad that 
practically screams at you: “Make $10K a month with my secret 
business blueprint!” The guru in the video stands in front of a 
rented Lamborghini, flashing screenshots of massive earnings. It 
looks… suspiciously easy. But hey, what if it actually works? 
You hover over the Buy Now button. For just $997, you could 
unlock the “secrets” to wealth. But do you even have that kind of 
money to spare? 
If you don't have enough Capital, you hesitate, realizing that 
throwing money at a random guru might not be the smartest 
move. Instead, you decide to: 
●​ Search for free resources and build your business 
from the ground up. → Go to 11

You decide to take your time, soaking up knowledge before 
making any major moves. You dive into books, podcasts, and 
YouTube videos on entrepreneurship. Each day, you pick up 
something new, how to craft an irresistible offer, the psychology 
behind pricing, and the importance of branding. You fill notebooks 
with ideas, sketch out potential business models, and build 
confidence in your expertise.

this knowledge, but no action. You realize that learning is only 
half the battle. You need to start implementing.

17. Direct Outreach – Making the First Move 
You decide that waiting for customers to come to you isn’t a 
strategy, it’s a gamble. Instead, you take matters into your own 
hands and start reaching out to potential clients directly. 
Maybe you cold DM people on Instagram or LinkedIn, or 
maybe you email small business owners who might need your 
services. Either way, you brace yourself for responses, or lack 
thereof. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → Success! A few people respond positively, and 
you land your first real business opportunity. → Go to 
58 
●​ 8-10 → Some interest, but no immediate sales. A few 
people respond, but most say "I’ll think about it." → Go to 
59 
●​ 7 or below → Rejection city. Most people ignore you, 
and the few who reply aren’t interested. → Go to 60 
Reaching out directly is tough, but it’s also one of the fastest 
ways to get momentum. The question is, how do you follow up 
from here?

You decide to skip the slow grind and get your business in front 
of potential customers fast by running paid ads. Facebook, 
Instagram, Google, you pick a platform, set a budget, and hit 
“Launch.” 
Now, you wait. Will your investment bring in sales, or will it vanish 
into the abyss of bad targeting and ignored ads?

down, optimize, or pull back? 
19. Validating Your Offer – Talking to Real 
Customers 
You realize that before you invest any more time or money, you 
need real feedback. It’s time to talk to potential customers and 
validate whether your offer is actually something people want. 
You put together a quick survey, hop on calls, or engage in direct 
conversations with your target audience. What they say could 
change everything.

●​ 11+ → Strong validation! People love your idea, and 
some even pre-order. → Go to 64 
●​ 8-10 → Mixed feedback. Some people like it, but others 
raise concerns. → Go to 65 
●​ 7 or below → Bad news. People don’t seem interested at 
all. Your idea needs serious work. → Go to 66

pages.rawText:
Validating your offer before launching could save you time and 
money, but it could also reveal hard truths about your idea.  
20. Crafting the Perfect Offer 
Armed with research from real customers, you sit down to 
create an offer they can’t refuse. Pricing, bonuses, and how you 
position it all matter. 
But will your research-driven offer hit the mark, or fall flat? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Nailed it! Your offer aligns perfectly with customer 
needs, and people are eager to buy. → Go to 67 
●​ 8-10 → It’s solid but needs work. Some people show 
interest, but it’s not converting as fast as you hoped. → 
Go to 68 
●​ 7 or below → Something is off. Maybe it’s the price, the 
messaging, or just bad positioning. → Go to 69 
A well-crafted offer is the difference between a struggling 
startup and a business that thrives.

and Selling Immediately 
Who needs research? Time is money, and while others waste 
hours on surveys, you take action. 
You craft an offer, set up a quick landing page, and start 
promoting immediately, no customer validation, no feedback 
loops, just pure execution.

23. Building on Early Success – Scaling or 
Stumbling? 
With your first sale in the bag, you feel unstoppable. The 
question now is: how do you turn this into something bigger? 
You have a few options. You could double down on what 
worked, tweak your strategy to improve conversions, or even 
try something completely new. 
But scaling too fast or without a solid foundation could also 
backfire. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Breakthrough! You refine your approach, and 
sales double almost overnight. → Go to 77 
●​ 8-10 → Some progress, but not explosive growth. You 
make a few more sales, but scaling is harder than 
expected. → Go to 78 
●​ 7 or below → Overwhelmed! You scale too quickly or 
inefficiently, leading to missed orders, refunds, or ad 
overspending. → Go to 79 
Every business owner faces this moment, play it safe, or push 
forward aggressively. 
 
24. The Cold, Hard Silence – Facing the Crickets 
You refresh your inbox. Nothing. You check your website 
analytics. Still nothing.

No money? No problem. Plenty of businesses have started 
with nothing, if you’re willing to hustle. 
34. Finding Your Niche – Passion or Profits? 
After soaking up every free business lesson available, you realize 
something: you need a niche. 
Sure, you could just sell anything, but that’s how you end up 
being the person pushing “high-ticket drop-shipping” courses at 
family dinners. 
No, you need to pick something people actually want. 
So, do you follow your passion, chase the money, or try to 
blend both? 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Perfect niche unlocked! You find an in-demand 
market that also excites you. → Go to 125 
●​ 8-10 → Decent choice, but not groundbreaking. You 
land on something viable, but it won’t make you rich 
overnight. → Go to 126 
●​ 7 or below → Total dud. You spend way too long 
researching and pick something no one actually wants. → 
Go to 127

pages.rawText:
Choosing the right niche is like dating, pick the wrong one, and 
you’ll spend years wondering why you didn’t just go with your 
first instinct. 
35. Creating Your First Product or Service – The 
MVP Approach 
After diving deep into free resources, you realize there’s only so 
much learning you can do before you actually build something. 
You don’t need a perfect product, you just need something good 
enough to sell. 
So, what will it be? A service you can offer? A digital product? 
Something physical? You whip out your notebook and start 
brainstorming. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → You create a simple but powerful offer. It’s clear, 
valuable, and people love it. → Go to 134 
●​ 8-10 → It’s okay, but not amazing. You make something 
solid, but it still needs refining. → Go to 135 
●​ 7 or below → Overcomplicated mess. You get stuck in 
perfectionism hell, spending way too much time 
making it “just right.” → Go to 136 
A good business starts with a good offer, but too much 
overthinking can kill momentum.

Crickets?

pages.rawText:
You realize that who you know can be just as important as 
what you know. So, instead of grinding away alone, you decide 
to put yourself out there and start building relationships. 
Maybe it’s joining an online community, attending networking 
events, or just sliding into LinkedIn DMs like a desperate 
intern. Either way, this is your shot to connect with the right 
people and open doors. 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You make the right connections. Someone 
offers a partnership, a key referral, or even a first paying 
client. → Go to 137 
●​ 8-10 → You meet some interesting people, but no 
major breakthroughs. You build relationships, but 
nothing turns into immediate cash. → Go to 138 
●​ 7 or below → Networking nightmare. You either say 
something embarrassing, end up in a group full of 
time-wasters, or just get ignored completely. → Go to 
139 
Networking can open doors or waste time, depending on who 
you meet and how you use those connections. 
37. Friendly Investors – Family and Friends Come 
Through 
You delivered a killer pitch, and a few people believe in your 
vision. Maybe it’s your uncle who always wanted to be an 
entrepreneur, your friend who made a bit of cash in crypto, or 
your parents who just don’t want to see you fail. 
Either way, you got the money. Now, you just have to use it 
wisely.

People You Know 
You got the money, but it wasn’t free. 
Maybe they want a percentage of your profits, maybe they 
keep calling to check on their investment, or maybe they 
expect repayment way too soon. 
Suddenly, your business partner is also your mom, and that 
comes with some serious pressure.

them off your back. → Go to 143

→ Go to 144

→ Go to 145

39. No Luck – Your Friends and Family Just Aren’t 
Buying It 
You pitched your heart out, but no one’s biting. 
Maybe they’re too skeptical, maybe they just don’t have the 
money, or maybe they just don’t believe you’re actually going 
to pull this off. 
Either way, you’re still broke, and now you need to figure out 
another way to fund your business. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Bootstrap even harder, cut every unnecessary cost and 
grind your way forward. → Go to 146 
●​ Seek out an investor or business partner who has 
money to contribute. → Go to 147 
●​ Try crowdfunding, see if strangers will back your idea. → 
Go to 124 
Rejection stings, but plenty of great businesses started with 
nothing. Time to get creative. 
40. Turning a Scam into a Strategy 
Surprisingly, not everything in the guru’s course was total 
garbage. Sure, most of it was motivational fluff, but you 
managed to dig out something useful, a niche selection trick, a 
better sales angle, or even just a solid marketing tactic.

42. A Total Waste – The Guru Got You Good 
You stare at your screen in disbelief. 
Every single module, every so-called "secret strategy," every 
"proven blueprint", all of it is useless. You might as well have 
paid $997 for a motivational speech from a guy standing next to a 
rented Lamborghini. 
And now, you're down almost a grand with nothing to show 
for it. 
This is the moment when most people quit. But you? You’re not 
most people. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Pivot fast, forget the course and find a real strategy. → 
Go to 155

●​ Go all in on free resources to make up for the loss. → 
Go to 157 
Sometimes, the best lesson in business is learning how to 
spot a scam.

43. The Pivot – Moving on from a Bad Investment 
You shake off the frustration. Yeah, you lost money. Yeah, the 
guru scammed you. But wallowing in it won’t get you your 
money back. 
Instead, you take what little knowledge you did gain and pivot. 
Maybe you switch to a different niche, adjust your offer, or 
simply focus on a smarter strategy. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Brilliant move! Your pivot is exactly what was 
needed, and customers start responding. → Go to 158 
●​ 8-10 → It helps, but it’s not a game changer. You gain 
some traction but still struggle to scale. → Go to 159 
●​ 7 or below → Bad pivot. You change too much, confuse 
your audience, and lose valuable momentum. → Go to 
160 
A smart entrepreneur knows when to pivot, but a bad pivot can 
be just as dangerous as staying the course. 
44. The Service Hustle – Selling What You Already 
Know 
No more fancy tactics, no more "secret formulas", it’s time to sell 
what you already know. 
You skip the fluff and start offering a service immediately. No 
website, no fancy branding, just straight hustle.

47. Turning Failure Into Authority – Make Your Loss 
a Lesson 
Your guru course disaster was embarrassing, but what if you 
turned it into an advantage? 
People love a comeback story, especially when it comes with 
valuable lessons. 
So, instead of hiding your mistake, you decide to lean into it. 
You create content about how you got scammed, what you 
learned, and how others can avoid the same mistake. 
Will your transparency win people over, or will they just see 
you as another failed entrepreneur? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → People love it. Your honesty builds trust, and 
suddenly, you’re the go-to person for business advice. 
→ Go to 173 
●​ 8-10 → Some engagement, but no major impact. A few 
people appreciate your honesty, but it’s not a game 
changer. → Go to 174 
●​ 7 or below → It backfires. Instead of building authority, 
you just look like another failed entrepreneur complaining 
online. → Go to 175 
Turning failure into credibility is an art, some people build 
empires on their losses, while others just end up as cautionary 
tales. Which one will you be?

48. The Power of Partnerships – Leveraging 
Someone Else’s Resources 
Your mentor reminds you: You don’t have to do this alone. 
Instead of struggling solo, you find someone with resources, 
connections, or capital, someone who needs your skills but 
doesn’t have the time or expertise to execute. 
A strategic partnership could shortcut your success, but will 
you find the right deal or just end up working for free? 
Roll 2d6 + Networking (NE): 
●​ 11+ → You land a perfect partner. They bring funding, 
resources, or distribution, and suddenly, your 
business takes off. → Go to 176 
●​ 8-10 → You get a deal, but it’s not ideal. You gain some 
benefits, but your partner takes more control than you 
expected. → Go to 177 
●​ 7 or below → Bad partnership. You end up doing most 
of the work for little to no reward. → Go to 178 
The right partnership can fast-track your success. The wrong 
one? Just another bad business decision.

got a valuable new contact.

to connect with the right people.

around. → Go to 186

on. → Go to 187

connection could open doors you never imagined.

for dogs.”

next big thing.​

breakthrough.​

58. The Follow-Up Game – Turning Interest into 
Sales 
Some people actually responded to your messages, which is a 
win in itself. 
The bad news? Most of them said “I’ll think about it” (aka, 
business limbo). 
Now, it’s time to follow up like a pro. But how? Do you go for 
the hard sell, build a relationship, or pivot to a different 
approach? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → You follow up masterfully. A few prospects 
convert into paying customers. → Go to 200 
●​ 8-10 → Some progress, but no major breakthroughs. 
A few leads stay interested, but no immediate sales. → 
Go to 201 
●​ 7 or below → You overdo it. Either you followed up too 
aggressively or just caught them at the wrong time. → 
Go to 18 
Sales is a long game, some people buy immediately, some take 
months, and some just ghost you forever. The trick is knowing 
when to push and when to move on.

Problem

convinced that a single word was the problem.

off than before. 
Panic-pivoting rarely works, but at least now you know what not 
to do.

87. Steady Progress – Slow, But in Control 
Things are running… fine. 
Not fireworks. Not crickets. Just slow, steady progress. You’ve 
fixed a few backend issues, improved your processes, and while 
you’re not going viral, you’re not stressed either. 
You’ve bought yourself breathing room, but you know this pace 
won’t take you to $10K anytime soon. 
Time to make a decision: Do you stay on this careful path, or is it 
time to be a little bolder? 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Take a bold risk and launch a new, higher-ticket offer. → 
Go to 245​
 
●​ Stick to what’s working and gradually grow your customer 
base. → Go to 168​
 
●​ Focus on long-term customer retention and referrals. → 
Go to 224 
88. Stuck in Setup Mode – Losing Speed 
You’ve spent so much time fixing systems, polishing automations, 
and perfecting onboarding that you forgot one important thing… 
to sell. 
The momentum you had? Gone. Website traffic is flat, your inbox 
is silent, and your ad account hasn’t seen activity in days. On the 
bright side, your backend is immaculate.

the iron’s hot or play it smart and refine first?

Your test run didn’t flop… but it didn’t exactly take off either. 
Some people liked what you offered, others had concerns, and 
a few just ignored it altogether. You’re getting useful feedback, 
but no real money yet. 
It’s a reminder that business isn’t just about launching, it’s 
about adjusting. 
No Capital gain or loss, just valuable lessons. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Use the feedback to refine your offer and make it 
irresistible. → Go to 19 
●​ Go back to direct outreach to find customers who 
actually want what you’re offering. → Go to 17 
You’ve got something with potential, but potential doesn’t pay 
the bills. Do you tweak the offer or find the right audience? 
91. False Start – The Test Flops 
Well… that didn’t go as planned. 
Your test run was supposed to give you a taste of success 
before fully committing. Instead, it gave you a harsh reality 
check. 
●​ Barely any interest. 
●​ No sales.

Spending Money 
Your mentor leans in and says, "If you don’t have money, you 
better have value."

someone’s audience. Whatever the deal, you’re betting on your 
ability to negotiate.

110. A Clear Path Forward – Refining for Growth 
You took the feedback, refined your approach, and suddenly… 
it’s working. 
Maybe it was adjusting your pricing, tightening up your 
messaging, or simply doubling down on what worked, whatever 
the reason, you’re seeing real progress. Sales are increasing, 
customers are engaging, and you’re no longer just throwing 
ideas at the wall hoping something sticks. 
For the first time, you feel like you’re actually building 
something sustainable. 
Now comes the big decision: Do you go all in and push for 
aggressive growth, or do you stabilize your systems to make 
sure you don’t scale too fast and collapse under your own 
success? 
Gain $2,000 in Capital.

business to the next level, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to strengthen your foundations before 
expanding, go to 230.

Mistake 
You thought you were making smart improvements, but instead, 
you ended up overcomplicating everything. 
Maybe you spent too much time tweaking your website, 
changing your offer for the tenth time, or chasing shiny new 
marketing strategies that led nowhere. Whatever the case, you 
realize too late that you’ve burned through time, energy, and, 
unfortunately, money without getting any meaningful results. 
Your frustration is hitting an all-time high. You’re tempted to scrap 
everything and start over, but deep down, you know that’s not the 
move. You’ve already put in too much effort to backtrack 
completely.

113. Learning from Failure – Turning Setbacks into 
Success 
The rejection stung, but instead of wallowing in self-doubt, you 
take a deep breath and analyze what went wrong. 
Maybe your messaging wasn’t clear. Maybe your pricing was off. 
Maybe you were targeting the wrong audience altogether. 
Whatever the reason, you don’t let it stop you, you adjust, pivot, 
and try again. 
And this time? Something clicks. 
People start engaging. Leads trickle in. A few sales roll through. 
It’s not an overnight explosion, but it’s proof that your idea has 
legs. 
The hardest part of entrepreneurship isn’t failing, it’s learning to 
fail forward. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
●​ → If you’re ready to double down on what’s working 
and push forward aggressively, go to 227. 
●​ → If you want to refine your business foundations 
before scaling, go to 230.

Moving 
You’ve adjusted. Tweaked. Tried new approaches. And… it’s 
helping. Sort of.

117. The Product Upgrade – Worthwhile Investment 
or Wasted Money? 
Instead of throwing money into ads, you double down on your 
product. After all, if it’s not good enough to retain customers or 
generate word-of-mouth, no amount of marketing will fix that. 
You invest in improvements: 
●​ Better packaging? Check. 
●​ Enhanced features? Of course. 
●​ A high-end version for premium buyers? Why not? 
The hope? A stronger product = higher conversions, happier 
customers, and long-term growth. 
Roll 2d6 + Creativity (CR): 
●​ 11+ → Smart move! Customers love the improvements, 
and sales increase significantly. Your offer stands out,

pages.rawText:
and you attract more high-value buyers. Gain $3,000 in

dramatically. Some customers appreciate the changes, 
but it’s not a game changer. Go to 105  
●​ 7 or below → Overkill. You spent too much time and 
money improving something customers didn’t really care 
about. Worse, your price increase scared off buyers. Go 
to 112  
A great product can turn customers into lifelong fans, but go 
too far, and you might end up fixing things that weren’t broken. 
118. Playing It Too Safe – When Caution Holds You 
Back 
You decide to sit on most of your loan, keeping it as a financial 
cushion so you don’t run out of money too quickly. Smart, right?

in case things go south. But here’s the thing… businesses don’t 
grow by playing defense. You need to take risks, invest, and 
actually put that money to work if you want to make more of 
it. 
Eventually, you realize that just sitting on capital isn’t a 
strategy, it’s a slow road to nowhere. You need to spend wisely 
to scale.

138. Slow But Steady – Building Relationships Over 
Time 
Networking is weird. Sometimes you meet exactly the right 
person at the right time, and sometimes, you just have a bunch 
of awkward small talk and vague promises to “collaborate 
someday.” 
This time, it’s the latter. 
You’ve definitely met some interesting people, maybe even 
future allies, but no one is throwing money at you just yet. Still, 
you’re planting seeds, and if you keep nurturing these 
connections, something might come of it later. 
For now, though, what do you want to do?

145. Sticking to the Plan – Hoping for Patience 
You decide to stick to your original plan and trust that your 
investor (aka your friend, uncle, or overly enthusiastic mom) will 
stay patient while you work on making the business a success. 
You stay focused, use the money wisely, and avoid any 
unnecessary stress… for now. 
But will they stay patient or start nagging you for updates 
every five minutes? 
Roll 2d6 + Resilience (RE): 
●​ 11+ → They’re totally chill. They trust you, stay 
hands-off, and even offer more support if needed. Gain 
$1,500 in Capital. → Go to 246 
●​ 8-10 → They check in occasionally, but nothing too 
stressful. As long as they see progress, they’re fine… for 
now. No Capital gain or loss. → Go to 247 
●​ 7 or below → Big mistake. They start pressuring you 
non-stop, demanding updates, asking about profits, and 
even hinting at wanting their money back soon. Lose 
$2,000 in Capital. → Go to 248 
146. Hardcore Bootstrapping – Making Every Dollar 
Count 
No money? No problem. 
You decide to fully embrace the bootstrapper lifestyle, cutting 
every expense that isn’t absolutely necessary. Forget fancy 
software, paid ads, or even that overpriced oat milk latte, you’re in 
full grind mode now.

Backer 
You need money, and you’re not giving up. If friends and family 
won’t invest, then it’s time to look elsewhere.

deep pockets that you and your business are worth betting on. 
But investors aren’t just handing out cash, you’ll need to 
impress them.

They offer you a fair deal, and suddenly, your business 
has fuel to grow. → Go to 31

process, or cutting out the fluff that doesn’t actually matter.

pages.rawText:
You’ve learned your lesson, you’re not about to go all in blindly 
and risk everything again. 
Instead, you take a smarter, measured approach. You test your 
strategy, analyze results, and make small adjustments before 
going all out. 
●​ Maybe you launch a small-scale marketing campaign 
instead of spending everything upfront. 
●​ Maybe you sell to a test group first, getting feedback 
before expanding. 
●​ Maybe you just want one more sign from the universe 
before committing fully. 
Either way, you’re playing it safe, but you’re still moving forward. 
●​ You carefully refine your approach and only scale up 
when you see proof that it works. → Go to 228. 
152: Refining the Formula – Small Wins Add Up 
You take what’s working and double down. Maybe you fine-tune 
your messaging, tweak your pricing, or just get better at delivering 
what you promised. 
At first, it’s slow. A few sales here, some engagement there. But 
over time, those small improvements start adding up. Suddenly, 
you’re not just trying, you’re actually making real progress. 
Gain $1,500 in Capital. 
What’s next? 
●​ Push for aggressive growth now that you’ve got some 
traction. → Go to 227

The right move isn’t always about going bigger, it’s about getting

153: Rethinking the Strategy – Time for a New 
Approach 
Something’s off. No matter how much you tweak and test, this 
strategy just isn’t delivering the results you need. Maybe the 
market isn’t responding, maybe the competition is too strong, or 
maybe you’re just plain tired of forcing something that doesn’t feel 
right. 
Instead of banging your head against the wall, you decide it’s 
time for a fresh perspective. 
What’s next? 
●​ Pivot your offer, adjust what you’re selling to better 
match demand. → Go to 20 
●​ Shift your marketing strategy and try reaching a 
different audience. → Go to 116 
●​ Take a step back, review your data, and analyze 
what’s not working. → Go to 111 
Sometimes, success isn’t about pushing harder, it’s about 
knowing when to change direction.

pages.rawText:
Burnout is real. You’ve been grinding non-stop, testing strategies, 
making adjustments, and pushing forward… but something feels 
off. Instead of running yourself into the ground, you decide to take 
a step back, breathe, and regroup. 
It’s not quitting, it’s strategizing. 
●​ If you have The Bootstrapper as your mentor, they 
remind you that hustling smart is better than hustling 
hard. Gain $500 in Capital for making a calculated 
decision. 
After a short reset, what’s your next move? 
●​ Re-evaluate your approach and refine your current 
strategy. → Go to 111 
●​ Explore a completely new angle to market your offer. 
→ Go to 116 
●​ Reignite your motivation and push forward with fresh 
energy. → Go to 20 
Even the best entrepreneurs know when to step back and reset, 
it’s how you come back stronger. 
155. Pivot Fast – Cut Your Losses and Find a Real 
Strategy 
Enough is enough. You’re done chasing fake gurus and magic 
formulas. If you’re going to make this work, it’ll be on your own 
terms. 
You take a step back, rethink your approach, and start focusing 
on real business fundamentals. No more get-rich-quick nonsense, 
just solid strategy and execution. 
128

Sure, you've blown almost five grand on a course that's about as 
useful as a chocolate teapot. But that one connection from the 
Inner Circle, now they're the real deal. 
Your new pal casually mentions they're friends with some big 
industry names, and you suddenly feel like you just found the 
golden ticket at the bottom of your dumpster fire purchase. 
Inspired by your mentor's wisdom ("Networking is just 
professional flirting, do it right and you'll never be broke again"), 
you carefully nurture this promising connection, playing it cool, 
friendly, and not at all desperate. (Okay, maybe just a little 
desperate.) 
​
 Gain +1 to Networking (NE). 
With your shiny new contact ready to open doors, what’s your 
next move?

collaboration or partnership. → Go to 137

people in your industry. → Go to 102 
●​ Casually ask your new friend for a warm introduction to 
potential clients. → Go to 36​

guidance instead of judgment (though you'll happily take either at 
this point).

"If I never think about it again, did it really happen?" you muse 
philosophically, staring mournfully at your empty bank account. 
But ignoring a disaster doesn’t mean it didn’t happen. While you 
can pretend all you want, your wallet won't forget anytime soon. 
It’s time to rebuild, minus your dignity and five grand. 
What’s your next (less embarrassing) move? 
●​ Quickly pivot to a low-risk service-based offer, aiming to 
earn back your lost cash before anyone notices. → Go to 
44​
 
●​ Use humor and brutal honesty to share this epic fail 
online, turning your costly mistake into viral content. → Go 
to 47​
 
●​ Double down and reinvest carefully in market research, 
determined not to make the same mistake twice. → Go to 
19 
188. Strike While the Iron is Viral 
With your recent social media hit buzzing, you quickly put 
together a fresh offer to capitalize on your newfound attention. 
After all, the internet has the attention span of a caffeinated 
squirrel, blink, and they might move on. 
You craft a quick sales page, whip together a catchy headline, 
and pray to the marketing gods that the likes turn into actual 
cash. 
It's time to see if your viral moment translates into sales or fades 
like yesterday’s trending hashtag.

Payments ping your notifications, prospects become customers,

close even more prospects. → Go to 74​

future leads close faster. → Go to 141​

201. Still on the Hook – Interest, But No Payday 
(Yet) 
Your follow-up strategy wasn’t exactly a flop, but it’s not filling 
your wallet either. Several leads politely promise they're "still 
considering," which feels suspiciously like being gently 
friend-zoned in business terms. 
Frustrating? Absolutely. Hopeless? Not yet. 
Maybe they're truly interested and just slow to commit, or maybe 
they're politely ghosting you. Either way, your sales funnel 
currently feels more like a sales sieve. 
What’s your next move to break this awkward stalemate?

203. Message Makeover – Saying It Better 
You take a hard look at your outreach messages and realize… 
yeah, they kind of suck. 
Too formal? Too vague? Too “Hi, I help entrepreneurs 10x their 
thing with synergy”? Either way, it’s time for a full-on makeover. 
Armed with a clearer value proposition, punchier copy, and a little 
personality, you hit send on a fresh round of outreach. It’s still 
cold… but at least it doesn’t feel like a corporate bot wrote it. 
Responses start rolling in, slower than you’d like, but warmer than 
before. 
What do you do next? 
●​ Double down and send your new messaging to a bigger 
audience while momentum is building. → Go to 116​
 
●​ Start nurturing the best leads you’ve gotten so far, building 
deeper relationships to close them. → Go to 58​
 
●​ Mix in another approach, content, ads, or networking, to 
avoid relying solely on outreach. → Go to 140​

You manage to put off your lender, buying yourself a little 
breathing room.

pages.rawText:
You’ve struck gold with your offer. Now it’s time to fan the flames 
and see how far this thing can go. 
You throw more money into ads, crank up your email campaigns, 
maybe even DM a few influencers to see if they'll bite. It’s not just 
about getting more eyeballs, it’s about turning that attention into 
serious revenue. 
Now let’s see if your scaling gamble takes you to the moon or just 
mildly singes your eyebrows. 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Rocket-ship mode engaged! Sales skyrocket, and 
your brand starts picking up serious buzz.​
 Gain $4,000 in Capital. → Go to 240​
 
●​ 8–10 → Steady climb. You scale successfully but not 
explosively. Still, it’s working, and profit is growing.​
 Gain $1,500 in Capital. → Go to 241​
 
●​ 7 or below → Oof. Scaling too soon backfires. Costs rise, 
conversions dip, and the numbers don’t look so pretty.​
 Lose $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 242 
216. Deliver the Goods – Building Trust and 
Systems 
Your offer crushed it, now comes the part where you actually 
have to fulfill it. Time to swap hype for hard work. 
You onboard customers, answer questions, deliver value, and fix 
things on the fly (including that one broken link in your welcome 
email… oops). It’s a bit chaotic, but you handle it like a pro.

Instead of sprinting ahead, you pause. 
You revisit your onboarding process, clean up your automations, 
tighten your support systems, and fix that weird bug that sent five 
people the same welcome email (oops). It’s not flashy, but this is 
the kind of work that prevents disaster after you scale. 
When you finally press the gas, everything runs smoother. Fewer 
fires. Happier customers. More repeat business. 
You might not feel like a rockstar right now, but future you is 
silently high-fiving your decision. 
Gain $2,500 in Capital. 
What’s your next move? 
●​ Confidently scale now that your backend is solid. → Go to 
205​
 
●​ Launch a second offer while everything’s running 
smoothly. → Go to 54​
 
●​ Double down on retention, turn new customers into raving 
fans. → Go to 216 
221. Close the Gap – Making the Offer Irresistible 
You've got attention, but no sales. Like being popular at a party 
and still leaving alone. 
Time to get serious. You refine your messaging, tighten your 
call-to-action, clarify the value, and maybe even adjust the price. 
You replace “transformational” with actual benefits. Your new 
goal? Less hype, more conversion.

You’ve had enough of slow progress. No more polite marketing or 
playing it safe, you’re swinging for the fences. 
You launch a bold campaign, revamp your brand, invest heavily in 
paid ads, or maybe even pitch a risky new offer. It’s high-stakes, 
high-reward, and there’s no turning back. 
This is either the breakthrough you’ve been waiting for… or the 
moment everything falls apart.

responds, and the momentum you dreamed of finally kicks 
in →  Gain $4,000 in Capital. Go to 240​

overall you move forward.​

234. The Deal From Hell – Trapped in a Toxic 
Partnership 
At first, it felt like a dream: funding, support, maybe even a little 
mentorship. 
But now? It’s a waking nightmare. 
Your new partner constantly second-guesses you, rewrites your 
emails, and once tried to “optimize” your funnel by replacing your 
CTA with emojis. Worse, they hold equity, so you can’t just kick 
them out. 
You’re stuck navigating egos, delays, and “synergy” meetings that 
somehow achieve nothing. It’s exhausting. 
Lose $2,000 in Capital (burnout, missed opportunities, damage 
control). 
Now it’s time to claw your way out, or find a way forward despite 
the chaos. 
What’s your next move?

deeper.

Wrong

your bank account started sweating.

Facebook is secretly trolling you.

another dollar. → Go to 208​

strategy. → Go to 196​

77​

shut down your ads, pause new orders, and send out a heartfelt 
“we’re fixing things” update to your customers.

256: The Flash Promo – Bold Move, Fast Action 
Enough thinking. Enough planning. You throw together a promo 
in record time, tight deadline, juicy bonus, just enough urgency to 
snap people out of scroll-mode. 
It’s not perfect, but it’s out there. Now you wait… and refresh… 
and wait again. 
Did the bold move pay off, or did your audience just blink and 
scroll past? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Boom! Urgency works. Buyers rush in, and you get 
a burst of sales and fresh momentum.​
 Gain $2,500 in Capital. → Go to 270​
 
●​ 8–10 → A few bites. It doesn’t go viral, but you make 
some money and break out of the funk.​
 Gain $1,000 in Capital. → Go to 271​
 
●​ 7 or below → Crickets. Maybe it felt rushed. Maybe 
people didn’t care. Either way… ouch.​
 Lose $500 in Capital. → Go to 273

What’s killing your conversions? Bad headlines? Confusing offer? 
Too many steps between click and checkout? You dig into the 
numbers like a detective solving a sales murder mystery. 
Eventually, it clicks. You spot something, an obvious tweak, a 
misaligned message, or a missing trust trigger. It’s fixable. 
No fireworks. No viral breakthrough. Just a solid improvement to 
your system that might change everything. 
Gain $1,000 in Capital. 
What now? 
●​ Relaunch with a more streamlined funnel and updated 
messaging. → Go to 77​
 
●​ Layer in a bonus or scarcity element to increase urgency. 
→ Go to 256​
 
●​ Focus on retention, maybe the problem isn’t traffic, but 
customer value. → Go to 224 
258: The Comeback – Turning Pressure Into Profit 
You hit send, publish, post, and pray. 
Then… a ping. Then another. And another. Sales start rolling in 
like you just dropped a Black Friday deal with 1-minute shipping. 
It’s not just the cash, it’s the validation. Your audience wanted 
what you had. You didn’t just survive the pressure… you used it 
as fuel. 
You clear your debt. You breathe. You’re back.

260: Hitting $10K – Almost There! 
You’re exhausted. The bold launch? It flopped. 
Refunds trickled in. Engagement fizzled. The pressure didn’t 
break you, but it bent you hard. You’re tired, overextended, and 
down to your last move. 
Still, you haven’t lost it all. You’ve got a product. A platform. A 
pulse. And you’re closer to your goal than you’ve ever been. 
You’re standing at the edge of the $10K cliff. One wrong step, and 
you’ll fall… but one smart move, and you might just fly. 
Lose $2,000 in Capital. 
What now? 
●​ Go all in on one final growth push. → Go to 270​
 
●​ Slow down and fix what’s not working before making 
another move. → Go to 271 
261: Stuck at the Finish Line – Struggling to Break 
Through 
You’re so close you can taste it… but everything feels harder 
now. 
Sales have slowed. Your inbox is a mix of half-interested leads 
and people asking for refunds. You’re patching holes, chasing 
invoices, and trying to stay motivated with “motivational reels” that 
just make you want to scream into a pillow. 
You're not failing, but you're not winning yet either.

268. The Quick Discount – Desperate or Smart? 
Frustrated that people are hesitating, you throw in a limited-time 
discount or bonus to push them over the edge. It’s a quick fix, but 
will it boost conversions, or just cheapen your offer? 
Roll 2d6 + Tactics (TA): 
●​ 11+ → Nailed it. The urgency works, and fence-sitters 
finally convert. Gain $2,000 Capital. → Go to 270​
 
●​ 8–10 → A modest bump. You get some buyers, but 
margins shrink. Gain $500 Capital. → Go to 271​
 
●​ 7 or below → Backfire. People still don’t buy, and now 
they think your product isn’t worth full price. Lose $1,000 
Capital. → Go to 273 
​
269: Chasing Shadows – The Desperate Replay 
Instead of fixing the root problem, you keep pushing the same 
weak offer, convinced you just need more eyes on it.​
​
At first, you get a few clicks. Maybe even a polite “looks cool” DM. 
But sales? Nothing. The more you push, the more desperate you 
look, and your audience can smell it. 
●​ Lose all Capital (your savings and ad spend vanish 
chasing a dud) & restart from Section 1.

Strike Twice 
You take your viral post and pump it straight into ads. Surely, if 
people loved it organically, they’ll love it with money behind it… 
right?

The audience is different, the vibe is different, and suddenly your 
once-brilliant post is just another ad people scroll past. Your 
budget evaporates while you chase a ghost of past success. 
Lose $1,000 in Capital.​

Now what?

to 196​

→ Go to 227

You did it. 
You clawed your way through shady gurus, broken funnels, failed 
launches, awkward DMs, and more caffeine than any doctor 
would recommend… 
And now? You’ve made $10,000 in Capital. 
You’ve gone from side-hustler with a dream to a business owner 
with results. 
Now comes the real challenge: scaling beyond $10K without 
losing your sanity, your audience, or your edge.

You were right there. The $10K milestone in sight. One final push 
was supposed to be enough. 
But the universe had other plans. 
Maybe it was a surprise refund, a stalled ad campaign, or your 
checkout page glitching at the worst possible time. Whatever it 
was, it cost you, just enough to delay your finish. 
You’re not out. You’re not broken. But now you’ve got to regroup, 
re-strategize, and prepare for your final move. 
Lose $500 in Capital.

284. The Final Make-or-Break Moment – All or 
Nothing 
You’ve fought your way through the first stage of your business. 
The endless late nights, second-guessing, and awkward cold 
emails. The tiny wins that kept you going. The "What the hell 
am I even doing?" moments that nearly made you quit. 
But now, you’ve hit the wall. 
You’re not quite at the $10,000 mark. You’ve come close, but 
close doesn’t pay the bills. 
There’s only one way forward. 
It’s all or nothing. 
One final gamble to determine if you break through to the next 
era of your business or watch your business collapse before 
it even begins.

choices shape your fate:

riches.​
 
●​ You might take a cautious route, eking out survival until 
fortune smiles again.​

where chance decides whether your idea soars or 
belly-flops into the abyss.​

the stat listed, Creativity, Tactics, Resilience, Networking, or Tech 
Savviness.

●​ 8-10 is mixed: success tinged with cost or compromise.​
 
●​ 7 or less is failure: Capital vanishes, momentum shatters, 
and you must pick yourself back up.​

world of business. Bold gambles may pay off, or ruin you. Careful 
choices may keep you safe, but rarely lead to glory.

pages.rawText:
Capital is the beating heart of your journey. Think of it as both 
your treasure chest and your life bar. Each coin you earn or lose 
represents the tide of your business fortunes. 
●​ You begin with $1,000 Capital.​
 
●​ Sections may grant you Capital (sales, victories, 
investments) or take it away (bad hires, wasted ad spend, 
trolls).​
 
●​ If your Capital ever falls to zero, your business collapses, 
your story ends, and you must return to the beginning to 
try again.​
 
●​ If you reach $10,000, you have proven yourself worthy 
and move to section 280.​
 
Remember: money here is not a score. It is blood in the veins. 
Treat it recklessly, and you may bleed out. Guard it wisely, and it 
may grow into the fortune you seek.

pages.rawText:
Their backstory is one of grinding, hustling, and building empires 
out of coffee-stained notebooks and second-hand laptops. 
They’ve been through the storms, bad launches, zero-dollar 
months, trolls in the inbox, and lived to tell the tale. And now, 
they’ll teach you how to do the same. 
The Bootstrapper isn’t glamorous. They’re not flashy. They’re not 
the one sipping cocktails in Bali while posting “#CEOlife.” They’re 
in the trenches, grinding out results, keeping costs low, and 
stacking small wins until they snowball into success. 
If you’re the kind of player who wants to play it smart, lean, and 
calculated, the Bootstrapper is your perfect first mentor. 
 
What They Offer 
Passive Ability: Frugal Mastery 
●​ You’ve learned how to make every dollar count. Gain +1 
Resilience (RE) permanently while The Bootstrapper is 
your mentor. You also reduce every Capital loss by $100.​
 
Once-Per-Act Power: Shoestring Miracle 
●​ When you hit a major failure roll (6 or below) and would 
normally lose Capital, you may instead roll again. On the 
second roll, you ignore the Capital loss, even if you still 
fail. The Bootstrapper knows how to patch the holes and 
keep you alive another day.​

The Bootstrapper’s Wisdom 
●​ “Your first office? It’s your bedroom. Deal with it.”​
 
●​ “If you can’t sell it with duct tape, Canva, and a free trial, it 
probably wasn’t worth selling.”​
 
●​ “Remember: Amazon started in a garage. Your business 
doesn’t need to look perfect. It just needs to survive.” 
The Hustler 
“Sleep is for the weak. Coffee is for the hustlers.” 
The Hustler is pure energy bottled up in human form. They’re the 
entrepreneur who will cold DM 200 strangers before breakfast, 
pitch three new offers by lunch, and still be scheming at 2 AM. ​
​
Subtlety? Never heard of it. Perfection? That’s procrastination in 
disguise. 
Their backstory is one of clawing their way up from nothing with 
nothing but relentless drive. They’ve been ghosted, rejected, 
laughed at, and told to “get a real job” more times than they can 
count. But every ‘no’ was just fuel. Every slammed door made 
them knock harder on the next one. And eventually, all that 
grinding turned into wins. 
The Hustler isn’t polished. They’re not the type who waits for 
perfect branding or a shiny funnel. They thrive in chaos, live off 
momentum, and believe that volume beats precision every single 
time. If you want to learn how to sell, survive, and thrive with 
sheer force of will, the Hustler is your mentor.

Funnel

pages.rawText:
Not for baking cakes. A funnel is the path customers take from 
“I’ve never heard of you” to “shut up and take my money.” Wide at 
the top, narrow at the bottom. 
 
Conversion 
When someone does what you wanted, signs up, buys, clicks, 
books a call. Every yes is a conversion. 
 
Traffic 
People coming into your business world, website visitors, social 
media followers, ad clicks. Without traffic, your funnel is just an 
empty tunnel. 
 
CPC (Cost Per Click) 
How much you pay each time someone clicks your ad. High CPC 
= your ad isn’t connecting. Low CPC = you’re doing something 
right. 
 
CPA (Cost Per Acquisition) 
The cost to actually acquire a customer. If it costs you $100 to sell 
a $50 product, you’ve got a problem.

pages.rawText:
ROI (Return on Investment) 
Did your money work harder than you, or did it just disappear? 
ROI measures if what you spent brought back more than it cost. 
 
Lead 
A potential customer. They’ve shown interest but haven’t opened 
their wallet yet. Leads are like dates, you’re not “official” until the 
sale. 
 
Niche 
Your chosen corner of the market. Dog training for busy parents, 
vegan fitness for over-40s, productivity for night owls, your niche 
is your territory. 
 
Organic Marketing 
The free route. Social posts, blogs, videos, word of mouth. Costs 
less cash, but more time and patience. 
 
Paid Ads 
When you rent attention instead of earning it. Facebook, Google, 
TikTok, pay them, and they’ll show your stuff to strangers.

Likes, comments, shares, messages. Engagement is how your 
audience shows they care. No engagement = shouting into the 
void. 
 
Evergreen 
Content, funnels, or offers that keep working long after you set 
them up. Evergreen = not tied to a holiday, launch, or trend. 
 
Launch 
A big push to sell, timed campaigns with deadlines, bonuses, and 
hype. Done right, a launch feels like fireworks. Done wrong, it’s 
more like a damp sparkler. 
 
Upsell 
The classic “want fries with that?” Selling something extra after 
the first purchase. Upsells boost profit without needing new 
customers. 
 
Backend 
The follow-up money machine. High-ticket coaching, 
memberships, or add-ons sold after the first offer. This is where 
the real profits often hide.

How much money a single customer spends with you over their 
entire relationship with your business. High LTV = a customer 
worth keeping.

When you work yourself into the ground chasing business growth. 
In the game, you lose Resilience. In real life, you end up crying 
over spreadsheets at 2 a.m. 
 
 
That’s it. You now speak fluent “marketer.” Don’t worry, you’ll pick

when you put the dice down. Business isn’t just theory, it’s 
practice. And now you’ve had a taste of what it feels like to run

This section is about turning lessons into action. 
1. Reflect on Your Journey 
Take five minutes and ask yourself: 
●​ Where did I shine? (Were you a natural closer, a creative 
genius, a resilient grinder?)​
 
●​ Where did I fail, hard? (Did tech rolls sink you? Did 
Resilience run out fast?)​
 
●​ What strategies would I do differently next time?​
 
This isn’t just about the game, it’s about understanding how you 
operate as an entrepreneur. Everyone has blind spots. The faster 
you spot yours, the faster you grow. 
2. Translate the Game into Real Business 
The dice rolls? That’s risk. The Capital gains and losses? That’s 
cash flow. The mentors? That’s the power of guidance. 
●​ If you failed because of money management, start 
tracking your expenses IRL.​
 
●​ If you thrived on Networking, maybe it’s time to hit a local 
event or DM that potential partner.​
 
●​ If Resilience saved you, ask yourself what habits keep you 
in the game when things go sideways.​

Every mechanic here mirrors real-world entrepreneurship. Treat 
your playthroughs like case studies. 
3. Pick One Action, Do It for Real 
You don’t need to build Rome tomorrow. But you do need to take 
one tangible action in the next 24 hours. 
●​ Write your first offer.​
 
●​ Create a simple landing page.​
 
●​ Send out 10 cold DMs.​
 
●​ Record a short video and hit “post.”​
 
Tiny actions stack into momentum. Don’t overthink it, just move. 
4. Replay (Seriously, Do It Again) 
The beauty of this book is that you can always start fresh. New 
character. New mentor. Different choices. Each run is another 
rehearsal for the real thing. You’ll discover patterns, develop 
instincts, and get comfortable with the uncomfortable. 
​

pages.rawText:
Not just through the pages of this gamebook, but through the 
gauntlet of choices, dice rolls, risks, and hard-won victories that 
mirror the real battlefield of business. 
Think back for a moment. You’ve stared failure in the face, 
laughed at disaster, clawed your way back from zero, and maybe, 
just maybe, built your first empire on the page. That’s not nothing. 
That’s the muscle memory of entrepreneurship. 
Now here’s the truth: this game was never really about Capital, 
dice rolls, or fictional trolls in your comments section. It was about 
you, your mindset, your ability to adapt, and the choices you 
make when things don’t go according to plan. 
And now comes the real ending, the part where you put the book 
down and decide whether the adventure stops here… or whether 
it’s just beginning. 
If you close the book and never take action, that’s fine, you had 
fun, maybe learned a thing or two, and rolled some dice. But if 
even one spark inside you is whispering “I could actually do 
this…” then you’ve already won. 
Because here’s the secret: you don’t need permission. You don’t 
need the perfect plan. You don’t need to roll double sixes to get 
started. You just need the courage to take the first imperfect step. 
So consider this your final decision point: 
●​ If you’re ready to step into the real world and build 
something of your own, turn to… your notebook, your 
laptop, your first customer. That’s where the next chapter 
begins.​
